events.title: Itasca Symphony: No Strings Detached
events.address: 720 NW Conifer Dr, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Grand Rapids' own Sam Miltich joined the Hot Club of San Francisco as a teenager and has since toured internationally and played Lincoln Center. This February he brings his band home to share the Reif stage with the Itasca Symphony Orchestra: Sam on guitar, his father Matthew Miltich on bass, plus other instruments. The music travels. Choro (SHOH-roo) is the quick, bright instrumental music of Rio de Janeiro. The Nuevo Tango from Argentina. Čoček (CHO-chek) is the Romani dance music of the Balkans. And Sam got his start in the swinging guitar jazz Django Reinhardt made famous in 1930s Paris. For the finale, young string players from IOSP's programs in Grand Rapids, Bigfork, and Remer join the band and the orchestra for one big celebration of music. It's a February night out of the cold, with musicians of every age on one stage.

events.title: Jaerv and OK Factor
events.description: Legendary Swedish group Jaerv and Twin Cities-based duo OK Factor return to the beautiful Sacred Heart alter stage Friday, Oct. 16. The award-winning Jaerv present an extroverted, vigorous and heartfelt folk music with influences from both jazz and pop music. The group offers a varied stage performance where five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. Jaerv is an internationally well known act and has toured the U.S., Japan, Spain, Scotland, Ireland, Finland and Norway among other countries. Their discography includes three full length albums. New classical crossover group OK Factor was formed more than 10 years ago by cellist Olivia Diercks and violinist Karla Peters. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh. The group has toured nationally, internationally and recorded five studio albums of original work. Advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Sept. 11. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 (Student rush $10) while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold album release concert
events.description: Duluth-based Americana group Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold celebrate the release of their new album “Dedication.” Steeped in musical traditions of folk, bluegrass, country, classic rock, and blues, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold offers a genre-blending sound that is captivating, invigorating, and sure to get your toe tapping. After two decades of writing songs and performing as a solo artist, Danny Frank released of his debut album “Smoky Gold” in 2021. He then assembled an all-star cast of seasoned musicians to fully compliment his music. “The Smoky Gold” is comprised of banjo player Harrison Olk (Tin Can Gin, Cascade Crescendo, Kind Country Band), bassist Joe Scarpellino (Smokin’ Joe, Dead Larry), and fiddle savant Erin Aldridge (Concert Master – Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra). Together the group has recorded and released the full length album “Dedication.” Opening the evening will be Adam Greuel (Horseshoes & Hand Grenades) and Kenny Leiser (Joseph Huber). Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $20 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $20 (plus $1 handling fee). Tickets will be available at the door for $25 while supply lasts. Doors at 6 :30 pm. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.description: The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. Perfect for the Halloween season, “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is spooky, stylish and historically significant. It is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. This masterpiece influenced later film directors such as Alfred Hitchcock and Tim Burton. Attendees are encouraged to come dressed for Halloween, adding to the film’s haunted atmosphere. Aaron David Miller returns to Sacred Heart Music Center to accompany this film on the Center’s outstanding Felgemaker pipe organ. Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country. Advance adult tickets are $20 (plus a $3.18 handling fee) and are available on Eventbrite HERE. Tickets will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. All students can pay $5 at the door. Doors at 6 pm. Show at 7.

events.title: Black Parade Duluth – A My Chemical Romance Tribute
events.description: Duluth artists celebrate the 20th anniversary of My Chemical Romance’s classic album “The Black Parade.” Considered an emo rock masterpiece, the concept album “The Black Parade” is a career defining work from American rock band My Chemical Romance. The full album will be performed by an all-star Duluth band featuring members from Jumpsuit, Between Howls, Gemstones, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold, The Draco Volans, Duluth Transit Authority, and many more. Duluth-based Ephemera opens. Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $15 (plus $2.85 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $15 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $15 (plus $1 handling fee). Tickets will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30 pm. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love. Duluth-based singer-songwriter and bandleader Breanne Marie of Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners will open with a solo set. Advance E-tickets are available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund. Advance E-tickets will be available for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Thursday, Oct. 1. Paper tickets will be available for $20 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $25 while supply lasts. Doors at 6. Music at 7.

events.title: The Last Revel
events.description: Minneapolis-based The Last Revel brings its exciting Americana-folk sound to the beautiful Sacred Heart altar stage at 7:30 pm Thursday, Jan. 14. Duluth-based eerie-folk quintet Superior Siren opens. Formed in 2011, The Last Revel uses traditional folk-minded three part harmonies with honest and meaningful lyrics to deliver a passionate and soul stirring performance. The group has released six full length albums and will celebrate the 10th anniversary of its landmark “Hazard & Fate” album. Their latest, “Gone For Good,” was produced by Dave Simonett of Trampled by Turtles. General admission advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Oct. 2. General admission paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). General admission tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts.

events.title: “The Librarians” Documentary Screening
events.description: Please join the Kathryn A. Martin Library for a screening of the documentary, The Librarians, as well as a banned books discussion panel. Located in Bohannon Hall 90 on the UMD Campus. ABOUT THE FILM Librarians emerge as first responders in the fight for democracy and our First Amendment Rights. As they well know, controlling the flow of ideas means control over communities. In Texas, the Krause List targets 850 books focused on race and LGBTQIA+ stories – triggering sweeping book bans across the U.S. at an unprecedented rate. As tensions escalate, librarians connect the dots from heated school and library board meetings nationwide to lay bare the underpinnings of a large-scale coordinated extremist movement fueling the censorship efforts. Despite facing harassment, threats, and laws aimed at criminalizing their work – the librarians’ rallying cry for freedom to read is a chilling cautionary tale. Runtime: 88 min. Free

events.title: Photography & Art at the Rock: Featuring Shawn Malone
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: September at the Rock celebrates the wonder of Lake Superior—by day, by night, and under the stars. We are proud to feature Shawn Malone, a landscape photographer and visual artist whose work has been inspired by the Lake Superior region for more than 25 years. After moving from Chicago to Marquette, Michigan, Shawn found both her home and her artistic calling along the shores of Lake Superior. Since then, she has dedicated her career to capturing the ever-changing beauty of this remarkable landscape—from rugged coastlines and dramatic weather to the brilliant colors of the aurora borealis and the quiet brilliance of the night sky. Best known for her immersive aurora and night sky photography, Shawn creates images and time-lapse films that reveal the beauty of the natural world in ways often hidden from the naked eye. Her work invites viewers to slow down, look up, and experience the wonder that unfolds after sunset. In addition to operating her Lake Superior Photo gallery in downtown Marquette, Shawn is an award-winning photographer, educator, and workshop leader. She has spent more than a decade sharing her passion for the night sky through presentations, photography workshops, and guided experiences throughout the Great Lakes region, helping others discover the magic of photographing Lake Superior under the stars. On display September 1–30. Meet the Artist: September 29 | 10 am–6 pm Experience Lake Superior through the lens of one of the region’s most accomplished night sky photographers.

This year’s hunt will feature clues associated with banned books, in celebration of National Banned Books Week October 4-10, 2026. events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion
events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. events.description: Join us for an evening of connection, community, and hope. On Thursday, October 15, from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., we’re transforming the Lake Superior Zoo into a glowing experience filled with luminary-lit pathways, live music, local food vendors, wellbeing activities, and opportunities to connect with others. Every light along the pathway represents hope, connection, and the positive impact we can make when we support one another. Through Project Horizon, Members is helping create opportunities that foster mental wellbeing, strengthen relationships, and inspire positive change throughout our communities. events.title: World Ballet Company: Swan Lake
events.description: TICKETS Get Tickets Here Make it a group experience! Special pricing is available for groups of 10 or more: worldballetcompany.com/group-tickets. ABOUT THE SHOW The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra! The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (including 20-minute intermission) Audience: For ages 5 & over ABOUT WORLD BALLET COMPANY World Ballet Company – Ballet Everywhere, Ballet For All. Based in Los Angeles, and led by Sasha Gorskaya and Gulya Hartwick, World Ballet Company presents the most beloved and iconic ballets of our time in cities nationwide. Driven by the belief that ballet is for everyone, performances appeal to newcomers and seasoned ballet goers alike. The company attracts many international artists and comprises renowned professional dancers representing over ten countries. To date, World Ballet Company has traveled to more than 300 cities, reaching an audience of more than 500,000 fans. WBC Website: https://worldballetcompany.com/duluth2 KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Hadestown
events.description: Hadestown, previously scheduled for March 16, 2026, at the DECC Symphony Hall, has been POSTPONED due to travel conditions and restrictions surrounding the Midwest Winter Storm. The performance has been rescheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. All current tickets will be valid for the October performance. ABOUT THE SHOW COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go. For more information, visit hadestown.com 2025-26 BROADWAY AT THE DECC SEASON LINEUP The Book of Mormon – October 28-29, 2025 A Magical Cirque Christmas – December 16, 2025 Tina – The Tina Turner Musical – February 15, 2026 The Music Man – April 29, 2026 Hadestown – October 19, 2026 BROADWAY AT THE DECC 2025-26 SEASON INFORMATION KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: History Happy Hour
events.description: Step into the 1920s for an evening of cocktails, hors d’oeuvres, music, and history at Glensheen! Begin your evening by entering through the Juliet Balcony, where you’ll be greeted with a cocktail and hors d’oeuvres before heading downstairs to explore Glensheen’s basement. Discover 1920s-inspired activities and artifacts on display, enjoy music from the era, snap a photo in the billiards room, and take in a few surprises along the way. Enjoy a selection of fun, 1920s-inspired cocktails available for purchase at the cash bar before settling in for an engaging history talk by local historian Tony Dierckins. Tony will present “Drying Out Duluth: From Temperance to Prohibition,” exploring Duluth’s complicated relationship with alcohol—from the city’s early liquor ordinances and temperance movement to Prohibition and the creative ways Duluthians continued to enjoy a drink. Following the talk, enjoy dessert and a special 1920s-themed experience to round out the evening. Dress to impress and embrace the spirit of the 1920s for this one-of-a-kind night at Glensheen. This event is for guests ages 21 and older. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. | Talk begins at 6:30 p.m. | Event ends at 9 p.m. Tickets: $45 Members | $55 Non-Members Purchase tickets at z.umn.edu/historyhappyhour

events.description: Three artists, one theme: explore Materials and Self at this Art Night Out featuring an artist talk with reclaimed materials artist Andrew Webster, found object painter Robb Quisling, and fiber artist Lauren Faherty. Enjoy snacks, beverages, and the three exhibitions on view starting October 19.

events.title: Neural Exercises for Autism, a conversation with the author
events.venue: At Sara’s Table Chester Creek Cafe
events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. Pastries will be provided for those who wish to partake, and beverages are guest responsibility. Our event is on a first come first serve basis. If you are unable to make it and register, please cancel as space is limited to the first 25 registrations.

events.title: Duluth Haunted Ship 2026
events.description: Welcome to the home of the William A. Irvin Haunted Ship Tours in Duluth, Minnesota! That hint of cool breeze you feel isn’t just a change of weather. Those are the spirits of the Duluth Haunted Ship swinging on anchor just outside your view. The ghouls on board are waiting to morph the William A. Irvin historic freighter into something truly sinister. This season marks the 31st year of this unhallowed event, starting Friday, October 2, 2026 and running long weekends through Halloween (plus MEA Wednesday, October 14, 2026). This year, you can look forward to more activity outside of the ship on Harbor Drive: enjoy food trucks every Friday & Saturday, lights, bonfires, drinks available for purchase, and more. Know Before You Go Avoid the General Admission (GA) line and buy a FAST PASS ticket. Enter through FAST PASS gate. General Admission tickets enter through the GA line. All tickets are valid for one tour. You may arrive anytime during open hours for the date that your ticket is valid. Tickets can be purchased at the gate. No child under the age of 12 will be admitted without a caregiver. The ship is not handicapped accessible. All sales are final. No refunds. events.title: 38 Special
events.description: Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots. “After all this time, we wanted to create a more modern 38 Special album,” says frontman and co-founder Don Barnes. “This is a fresh, updated approach to the sound we’ve been making together for so long. Why not make a big statement after all these years? When you’re reintroducing yourself to the world, ‘good enough’ doesn’t work anymore. If you’re gonna do it, you might as well go big.” Learn more at 38special.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: #IMOMSOHARD: The Flashback Tour
events.description: TICKETS Tickets on sale now! #IMOMSOHARD The Flashback Tour: Two moms, lots of laughs —creators of the popular web series and podcast on tour This is an age 18+ show. Saturday, November 7 | DECC Symphony Hall | 8:00pm Tickets on sale now! ABOUT THE SHOW #IMOMSOHARD began as a popular web series by real-life best friends, comedians, and moms, Kristin Hensley and Jen Smedley. One night, over a glass of wine and many tears of frustration, these two friends decided to tell a different kind of story. With a camera, two husbands, a babysitter, and bottomless mimosas, Kristin and Jen decided to speak openly about their fears and failures and to prove that the only way to survive motherhood is through laughter and friendship. The video was a smash hit, sparking an online community of two million of the most engaged followers – confirmation that moms and women everywhere need to laugh and be heard. KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Gary Owen
events.description: No Hard Feelings Tour TICKETS Tickets on Sale Now! ABOUT GARY OWEN Gary Owen has been entertaining audiences for more than two decades with his sharp observational humor and fearless storytelling. Known for his unapologetic, rule-defying style, his material draws from his personal life, time in the military and the everyday absurdities that connect people across backgrounds. With a fanbase that has grown by the millions in recent months and continues to surge across social media, Owen’s reach has cemented his place as one of the most in-demand touring comedians today. Beyond stand-up, Owen has appeared in a wide range of feature films including BACK ON THE STRIP with Tiffany Haddish and Wesley Snipes, MEET THE BLACKS and its sequel THE HOUSE NEXT DOOR, THINK LIKE A MAN and THINK LIKE A MAN TOO, RIDE ALONG with Ice Cube and Kevin Hart, LITTLE MAN opposite the Wayans Brothers, and DADDY DAY CARE with Eddie Murphy. He is also widely recognized for his scene-stealing role as “Bearcat” in the MGM film COLLEGE. On television, Owen starred in his own BET series THE GARY OWEN SHOW and co-hosted TruTV’s sketch series UPLOAD WITH SHAQUILLE O’NEAL. After meeting Tyler Perry on THE TOM JOYNER MORNING SHOW, he was cast in the recurring role of Zach the barber on the TBS comedy series TYLER PERRY’S HOUSE OF PAYNE. Owen continues to write, produce and perform his own groundbreaking comedy specials, including BLACK FAMOUS, #DOIN’ WHAT I DO, I GOT MY ASSOCIATES, I AGREE WITH MYSELF, TRUE STORY, URBAN LEGEND, and BREAKIN’ OUT THE PARK. Most recently, he recorded two specials back-to-back—BROKEN FAMILY and GARY OWEN...NO S, released this past spring on YouTube. In addition to his on-stage and on-screen work, Owen hosts his own podcast, #GETSOME WITH GARY OWEN, and has appeared on numerous others, including FLAGRANT PODCAST, TIGERBELLY, YOUR MOM’S HOUSE with Tom Segura & Christina P., CLUB SHAY SHAY and WE PLAYIN’ SPADES PODCAST with Nick Cannon, among others. ABOUT THE SHOW “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security. In 2004, Tyson was once again appointed by President Bush to serve on a nine-member commission on the Implementation of the United States Space Exploration Policy, dubbed the “Moon, Mars, and Beyond” commission. This group navigated a path by which the new space vision can become a successful part of the American agenda. And in 2006, the head of NASA appointed Tyson to serve on its prestigious Advisory Council, which guides NASA through its perennial need to fit ambitious visions into restricted budgets. In addition to dozens of professional publications, Dr. Tyson has written, and continues to write for the public. events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program. It does not guarantee you a parking space or specific seating at the event.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance. In his talk, Shawn uses research and case studies to show practical ways individuals and teams can surface the beliefs limiting them, reframe challenges as changeable, expand what they believe is possible and sustain those shifts under pressure. Register here for this virtual event: uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor Shawn Achor is the NYTimes bestselling author of The Happiness Advantage and The Power of Beliefs. Shawn graduated magna cum laudefrom Harvard and earned a Masters from Harvard Divinity School in Christian and Buddhist ethics. After spending 12 years at Harvard, Shawn traveled to 50 countries studying how to create an interconnected approach to potential and happiness.

events.title: The Oak Ridge Boys
events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment GET TICKETS HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution. Whether performing for presidents, recording fresh takes on their biggest hits, or exploring new musical directions with acclaimed producers, they bring the same passion that first propelled them to stardom. With decades of tradition, unmatched harmony, and a timeless catalog loved by generations, The Oak Ridge Boys continue to captivate audiences everywhere they go. Learn more at oakridgeboys.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Show a worker ID or pay stub for $1 off all Bent Paddle beverages. Thank you for keeping our paddles in the water! Everyone is welcome! Come for the tunes, stay for the conversations, delicious beverages, and good times. This month to kick off and celebrate the return, we invite you to connect with local organizations making waves in the Twin Ports — like WE Health, Trans+ Northland, Twin Ports Artists Collective, and Men As Peacemakers. Org’s may vary based on who available each week, but the good vibes are guaranteed!

events.title: Gobble Gallop
events.description: This Thanksgiving, join us for the Gobble Gallop — presented by Essentia Health. This 5K, 1-Mile, and Kids Run is Duluth’s favorite family tradition. Whether you’re racing or strolling, every step celebrates wellness, community, and the joy of moving together. Join us and be part of a Northland tradition that keeps hearts warm and feet moving! This event supports Safe Haven Shelter & Resource Center. A portion of the proceeds of the event as well as all partnership and participant donations go to helping Safe Haven continue their essential work in our community. The race starts between S. 12th Ave. E. and S. 13th Ave. E. on London Road, just outside the Rose Garden.

events.title: Prime Time at the Paddle: Meat Raffle & More
events.description: Join us at Bent Paddle for Prime Time at The Paddle, hosted by Skyline Rotary, a vintage tradition with a modern twist, all in support of a great cause. All proceeds from fundraising efforts go directly to the Rotary. Enjoy happy hour beverage specials, classic raffle fun, and plenty of chances to win loads of prizes. 7–9 PM | Every 4th Thursday of the Month Retro vibes. Prime Meats. Pure luck. Meat Raffle (vegan options available) Wheel Spin 50/50 Raffles Hosted by Rotary Open to the public event: We simply ask that you order beverages throughout the night and take good care of your friendly Beertenders! Meat at the paddle for a great cause and good time and if you’re lucky, you won’t leave empty handed!

events.title: Christmas at the Lighthouse Tours
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: ’Tis the Season—to Step Back in Time! Celebrate the holidays with a glimpse into winter life at Split Rock Lighthouse and discover Christmas traditions from the 1930s. Join a guided tour of the keeper’s home, help us decorate for the season, and learn how families celebrated the holidays nearly a century ago. As part of the experience, guests can create a vintage-style ornament to hang on the keeper’s Christmas tree or take home as a keepsake. It’s a festive way to start a new family tradition! **NOTE**: The tours take place from 10:30 AM – 11;30 AM, 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM, and 1:30 PM – 2:30 PM on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays except on 12/25

events.title: Duluth Winter Village
events.description: THE MAGIC RETURNS TO HARBOR DRIVE! Dates & Times: December 5–6, 2026 | Saturday & Sunday | 10:00 am – 4:00 pm Admission & Parking: FREE to attend! (DECC Parking is $10) AN EVENT UNLIKE ANY OTHER! For one weekend only, we’re bringing together the best of Duluth in one scenic location. The 10th annual Duluth Winter Village returns along the lake on Harbor Drive this December 5 and 6 from 10:00 am – 4:00 pm. The magic of local businesses, charming wooden shopping cabins, family-friendly activities, hot food, beverages (including beer & cocktails), and carolers continues to be a magical tradition. The festivities are held outside and inside at the Duluth Entertainment Convention Center. Visitors will appreciate: Our famous holiday-themed Experiential Bar “Tinsel Tavern” — featuring cocktails from Vikre Distillery Local makers & on-site Blacksmith Soup flights On-site holiday portraits by the Christmas tree Hollybeary Kid Store is back with more shopping options for littles to pick out for their grown-ups Animals, live caroling, 25-foot lit tree Small Children and Nursing Area by Duluth Mom Duluth Winter Village merch produced by our local vendors Hug-a-Hen by the Locally Laid Egg Company Lift Bridge, freighter views and bonfires The annual event began on the grounds of Glensheen Mansion in 2016 but moved to its new location in 2021. The Duluth Winter Village is unique from other area markets in that the vendors are all local businesses with retail locations around Northern Minnesota. Participants include Bailey Builds, Altered Abode, Y-ker Acres, Hucklebeary, Frost River, the Rainbow Room, NaturaLight, The Big Lake, Wintergreen Northern Wear, Lake Superior Art Glass, Ivy Moon and the Moon Market. Food and drink from the DECC’s culinary team, Positively Third Street Bakery, Hungry Hippie Tacos, Duluth’s Best Bread, Love Creamery, Scenic 61 by New Scenic Café, TBSP Waffles, Yes Cheese, and more. For more information, visit here.

events.title: Julebyen 2026
events.venue: 199 Alger Smith Rd, Knife River, MN 55609, United States
events.address: 199 Alger Smith Rd, Knife River, MN
events.description: 🎄 JULEBYEN 2026 – Scandinavian Nordic Christmas Village Festival 🎄 Step into the magic of a Nordic Christmas at Julebyen 2026, a one-of-a-kind holiday festival celebrating the traditions, culture, and festive spirit of Scandinavia! Join us on December 5–6, 2026 for a weekend filled with Christmas lights, holiday shopping, delicious food, family activities, live entertainment, and unforgettable winter experiences. ✨ Festival Highlights 🛍️ Outdoor Market, Fisherman’s Village & Heated Indoor Market 🚂 Heated train rides and scenic excursions 🎶 Live music and holiday entertainment throughout the grounds 🍲 Food vendors, food trucks, and Scandinavian-inspired treats 🎄 Beautiful Christmas displays and festive decorations 🧌 Trolls, gnomes, and Nordic folklore brought to life ⚔️ Viking-inspired exhibits and activities 🎁 Unique gifts from local artists, makers, and craftsmen ❄️ Family-friendly games, Hobby Horse Races, Activities, and Holiday fun Whether you’re searching for the perfect holiday gift, enjoying a warm meal with friends, taking a magical train ride, or making memories with your family, Julebyen offers something for every age. Bring your family, gather your friends, and experience a Christmas celebration inspired by the warmth, wonder, and traditions of the Nordic countries. 📅 Event Details Date: December 5–6, 2026 Time: December 5th 9am-4pm, December 6th 10am-3pm Location: Knife River, MN Sponsored by Lovin’ Lake County! 🎄 Fun for the Whole Family! Check out our web page julebyen.org for announcements, activity details, vendor spotlights, entertainment schedules, train ride information, and exciting updates as we count down to Julebyen 2026!

events.description: Ledge Rock Grille’s Blue Stuga at Julebyen’s Christmas Village is back! events.title: Creepmas Parade Duluth
events.description: The Creepmas Parade is an annual outdoor costume parade focused on folklore, blending Krampusnacht traditions and Creepmas aesthetics. Participants are encouraged to respectfully dress up as winter myths, cryptids or any creature that resonates with them. Bells are the unifying piece of the parade and organizers encourage everyone to jingle and jangle along the parade route. The parade takes place on the first Saturday in December. The parade can be joined at any point along the route. More information can be found at https://www.creepmasparadeduluth.com/

events.title: Fire and Frostbite

Our songs and artists change every show so you never know what might be in store! Support local queer drag artists and come see the colorful cast at The Caddy Shack, December 5th at 7pm Tickets: $10 (Cash Only) [ATM on Site] 21+ Event (ID’s Checked at Door) 2023 W Superior St, Duluth, MN 55806 https://caddyshackduluth.com/events/

events.title: A Christmas Story – Duluth
events.description: Get ready to embrace the holiday spirit with “”A Christmas Story – Duluth”” at the enchanting NorShor Theatre! Set in the heart of Duluth, Minnesota, this beloved musical brings to life the whimsical adventures of Ralphie and his quest for the ultimate Christmas gift. The NorShor Theatre, with its charming ambiance and rich history, provides the perfect backdrop for this heartwarming tale, ensuring that audiences of all ages will be captivated by the laughter, nostalgia, and festive cheer. Join us for an unforgettable evening filled with catchy tunes and delightful performances that will leave you humming long after the curtain falls. Whether you’re a lifelong fan or new to the story, “”A Christmas Story – Duluth”” promises to be a magical experience that will warm your heart this holiday season. Don’t miss out on this festive celebration—book your tickets now and make memories that will last a lifetime!

events.title: Arrowhead Ice Fishing and Winter Show
events.description: The Arrowhead Ice Fishing & Winter Show only comes once a year and it features a wide variety of new products and accessories. Whether you need an upgrade, or are totally new to the ice fishing scene, you will find what you are looking for at the biggest sale of the year. Bring the entire family and enjoy all of the festivities that the show has to offer. Dates/Hours Friday, December 11 – 12:00 pm – 7:00 pm Saturday, December 12 – 9:00 am – 7:00 pm Sunday, December 13 – 10:00 am – 4:00 pm For additional show information or to become an exhibitor, www.arrowheadiceshow.com

events.title: Minnesota Ballet | The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale
events.description: The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale offers a magical, local twist on the cherished holiday classic. As Clara’s Nutcracker doll comes to life, she embarks on a whimsical journey through a world filled with leaping lumberjacks, dancing gingerbreads, and swirling snowflakes, all set against Duluth’s charming landscape. The holiday tradition that leaves every audience spellbound — this season featuring Tchaikovsky’s beloved score performed live by the Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra. Friday, December 11 | 7:00 pm Friday Tickets Saturday, December 12 | 3:00 pm Saturday Tickets Sunday, December 13 | 3:00 pm Sunday Tickets More info: minnesotaballet.org

events.title: A Christmas Story – Duluth
events.description: Get ready to embrace the holiday spirit with “”A Christmas Story – Duluth,”” a delightful theatrical experience that brings the beloved tale to life at the iconic NorShor Theatre in Duluth, Minnesota. Set in a beautifully restored venue, the atmosphere is warm and inviting, perfect for families and friends looking to create lasting memories this festive season. Join Ralphie and his friends as they navigate the ups and downs of childhood, all while dreaming of the ultimate Christmas gift. This enchanting production promises to capture your heart with its charming performances and nostalgic storytelling. Whether you’re a long-time fan of the classic film or discovering the magic for the first time, “”A Christmas Story – Duluth”” is sure to leave you with a smile. Don’t miss out on this holiday tradition—book your tickets now and get ready for an unforgettable night at the NorShor Theatre!

events.title: Wild Santa 5k & Reindeer Run
events.description: This fun Saturday event winds through the Lincoln Park Craft District, beginning and ending at Wild State Cider. All you have to do is sign up for your 5-piece Santa suit to run in, a free cider (or juice), live holiday music and a free bowl of chili after the run. Kids 8 and younger can join the Reindeer Run for free. What can spectators expect? Hundreds of Santas running around the neighborhood.

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 4 – Across the Sea
events.description: Brace yourself for adventure as we explore the New World’s ties to the old. We set sail from Ancient Rome with Beethoven’s brooding Coriolan — a general destroyed by his own pride — before arriving in New Bedford, Massachusetts, heart of America’s whaling industry, with Stephen Paulus’ Sea Portraits. We close with Brahms, who poured the wreckage of his broken heart into one of the stormiest works in the repertoire. Featuring John Novacek, Piano BEETHOVEN Coriolan Overture PAULUS Sea Portraits BRAHMS Piano Concerto No. 1 Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

events.description: Join us for a delightful evening at the NorShor Theatre in Duluth, where the charming world of “”Emma – The Play – Duluth”” comes to life! This enchanting adaptation of Jane Austen’s beloved novel promises to whisk you away with its witty dialogue, vibrant characters, and a touch of romance. The historic atmosphere of the NorShor Theatre, with its stunning architecture and intimate setting, creates the perfect backdrop for this captivating tale of matchmaking and self-discovery. Whether you’re a long-time Austen fan or new to her work, “”Emma – The Play – Duluth”” offers something for everyone. Gather your friends and family for a night filled with laughter and heartwarming moments. Don’t miss your chance to experience this theatrical gem—book your tickets now and prepare for an unforgettable night at the theatre!

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 5 – In Sacred Light
events.description: A kaleidoscope of perspectives: “My Country ‘Tis of Thee”, filtered through Charles Ives’ shifting lenses. Fragments of a brilliant Schubert symphony left mysteriously unfinished. An old Lutheran hymn refracted and retold by Bach. A journey from light to darkness and back again, pieced together from a mosaic of sacred texts. Tonight’s program represents the American ideal of individual voices converging into one, unified whole. Featuring the DSSO Chorus and DSSYO Youth Symphony IVES Variations on “America” SCHUBERT Symphony No. 8, “Unfinished” BACH Cantata No. 4, Christ Lag in Todesbanden HAGENBERG Illuminare Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

events.title: NEEDTOBREATHE with special guest Conner Smith
events.description: Presented by Pepper Entertainment Sunday, February 21, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm TICKETS ON SALE NOW ABOUT NEEDTOBREATHE NEEDTOBREATHE is known for their distinctive blend of Americana, alt-rock, and spiritual depth—earning five No. 1 albums, over three billion career streams, sold-out tours, and a devoted global following. The South Carolina–bred group—Bear Rinehart, Josh Lovelace, Tyler Burkum, and Randall Harris—enters a new creative chapter with The Long Surrender, their tenth studio album and first release for MCA. events.title: Riverdance 30 – The New Generation
events.description: Sunday, March 14, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Roberts Group TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT THE SHOW Since Riverdance first emerged onto the world stage, its fusion of Irish and international dance and music has captured the hearts of millions worldwide. The Grammy award-winning music and the infectious energy of its mesmerizing choreography and breathtaking performances has left audiences in awe and established Riverdance as a global cultural sensation. To celebrate this incredible 30th year milestone, Riverdance will embark on a special anniversary tour, bringing its magic to audiences around the world. This spectacular production rejuvenates the much-loved original show with new innovative choreography and costumes and state of the art lighting, projection and motion graphics. And for the first time Riverdance welcomes “The New Generation” of performers, all of whom were not born when show began 30 years ago. John McColgan, Director of Riverdance said, “For over 30 years, Riverdance has taken us on a unique and exhilarating journey with the love and support of our audiences. The show has developed from a stage spectacle into a global cultural phenomenon. It has continuously evolved yet we ensure it always remains true to its roots. The 30th Anniversary showcases our “New Generation” of extraordinary talented performers with their electrifying energy, passion and skill in their traditions and their music and dance. Fresh, exciting and with all the magic and spectacle of the original, this is Riverdance better than ever before.” Audiences will enjoy a unique and memorable performance which blends the traditional and the contemporary, showcasing the skill and passion of the world-class of dancers, musicians and singers in the Riverdance ensemble. Composed by Bill Whelan. Produced by Moya Doherty. Directed by John McColgan. Learn more at riverdance.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: Echoes of Elegance: English Renaissance
events.description: Step back in time for an unforgettable afternoon of music at Fairlawn Mansion. Join us for a classical concert performed on beautifully preserved historical instruments, bringing the rich, resonant sounds of the past to life within the Mansion’s elegant surroundings. events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.venue: Virtual on Zoom: Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor to receive the Zoom link.
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance. In his talk, Shawn uses research and case studies to show practical ways individuals and teams can surface the beliefs limiting them, reframe challenges as changeable, expand what they believe is possible and sustain those shifts under pressure. Register at uwsuper.edu/ShawnAchor

events.title: Flashlight Tours of Fairlawn Mansion
events.description: Celebrate Spooky Season by taking a tour of Fairlawn Mansion after dark! This special guided tour takes place in the dark by lantern light. Our superstition experts will share Victorian superstitions, haunted history, and even their own paranormal experiences! This 30-minute tour takes you throughout all three floors of Fairlawn Mansion. You will see traditional Victorian era funeral and mourning decor, photographs, and even some artifacts from our own experiences of unexplained activity inside Fairlawn! 30 Minute tours starting at 6:30pm with the last tour departing at 9:30pm. Admission is $10/person. Tickets may be purchased at www.superiorhistoricproperties.org. Wear your Halloween costume for an even spookier experience! No full-face masks or inflatable costumes allowed and weapons are prohibited. There is no elevator at Fairlawn Mansion, so plan to wear comfortable shoes to climb stairs.

events.title: Pumpkin Land at Fairlawn Mansion
events.description: Kick off Superior Historic Properties’ Hallo-Week of Fun by visiting our brand new Pumpkin Land! This free outdoor event at the mansion is everything you need to get into the family-friendly Halloween spirit. Enjoy food trucks, live music from Born Too Late, games, pick-a-pumpkin, and a carving and decorating station to carve the pumpkin you picked out! To top it off, watch a demonstration from a pumpkin carving expert! There will be photo op areas throughout the lawn, so wear your best Halloween costume and snap a photo! Event Notes: For accessibility-related accommodations, email museums@superiorwi.gov. Pumpkins are picked on a first come, first served basis. While supplies last.

events.title: Open House: New Pruitt Center for Mindfulness and Well-Being
events.description: The University of Wisconsin-Superior invites students, faculty, staff and community members to an open house celebrating a new home for the Pruitt Center for Mindfulness and Well-Being and Student Health and Counseling Services. Guests are welcome to stop by throughout the afternoon to tour the newly renovated space, enjoy refreshments and meet faculty and staff from both departments. Student Health and Counseling Services provides counseling, psychiatric referrals and psychoeducation for students, while the Pruitt Center offers classes, trainings, workshops and resources that support positive mental health for students, UW-Superior employees and the greater community.

events.title: Trick or Treat in the District
events.address: Tower Ave to Broadway and all 89 blocks of the Superior BID
events.description: Spooky season is here so plan now to join us for Trick or Treat in the District! Participating SBID businesses offer treats for the kids and as always, fabulous shopping for the adults. For added fun and safety, a portion of Tower Avenue (14th through Broadway) will be closed to allow trick-or-treaters a safe way to cross between businesses. This is a free event sponsored by the Superior Business Improvement District.

events.title: Speaker Series - USS Indianapolis
events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: Join us as Paul Makowski delves into USS Indianapolis. This ship is famous for a top-secret mission to deliver atomic bomb parts in July 1945, followed by its tragic sinking by a Japanese submarine, which led to one of the worst shark-attack and survival ordeals in military history.

events.title: BOO Craft Market
events.description: Get ready for a spook-tacular day of shopping, and food!Join us on Saturday, October 10th from 9:00 AM - 3:00 PM at the Billings Park Civic Center in Superior, WI for the BOO Craft Market featuring 32 talented crafters and vendors offering unique handmade items, seasonal decor, gifts, clothing, tumblers, jewelry, baked goods, and so much more! This is a perfect time to start your holiday shopping!Whether you're looking for something spooky, cozy, handcrafted, or simply want to enjoy a fun day out, there's something for everyone at the BOO Craft Market!Admission is FREE! Food available for purchase.Bring your friends and family and spend the day supporting local makers while enjoying great food, festive fall vibes, and plenty of Halloween spirit. We can't wait to see you there!

events.title: Trunk-or-Treat at the Superior YMCA
events.description: Bring the family to the Superior YMCA for a free evening of Halloween fun at Trunk-or-Treat! Enjoy decorated vehicles, trick-or-treating, treats, and plenty of festive fun for the whole family. This event is free and open to the community. We hope to see you there!

events.title: Pearl Harbor Prophet
events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: A letter written to the White House by a man from Spooner, Wisconsin, forewarned of the details of the attack on Pearl Harbor 10 days before it happened. A local documentary film uncovers this fascinating story of how history was almost changed forever from right here in the Northwoods. Premiering on Veterans Day, 11/11/26, 6:15 pm at the Pearl Harbor Theater inside the Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center in Superior, Wisconsin. This event is free. Please reach out with any questions! This event is free.

events.title: indiGO Inclusive Hiring Business Lunch - A Community Conversation
events.description: Finding reliable work, keeping local businesses thriving, and building strong career paths takes a full community. What if one of the most effective solutions to our regional workforce shortage was sitting right here in Douglas County, waiting for us to collaborate?indiGO, in proud partnership with the Wisconsin Board for People with Developmental Disabilities (WI-BPDD), invites you to an inclusive regional dialogue open to the public designed specifically for employers, managers, and HR professionals:🤝Inclusive Hiring – A Community Conversation📅Date:Tuesday, October 13, 2026⏰Time:11:00 AM – 1:00 PM(A free meal is provided to all registered attendees!)📍Location:Superior Public Library, 1530 Tower Avenue, Superior, WIWhy you should attend:Whether you are a local business owner looking to optimize your workplace, a student or job seeker eager to connect, an educator guiding youth, or a resident invested in our local economy, your voice is needed at the table.This interactive public workshop will focus on:Our Shared Workforce Pool:Unlocking career pipelines that seamlessly integrate working-age transition students and emerging young adults into our local economy.Customized Employment Strategies:Discovering how businesses can optimize daily operations by matching candidate strengths with workplace needs.Community Resources:Navigating state hiring incentives, tax credits, and supportive workplace assistance provided through our coordinated local agency networks.Let’s turn data into local economic action. Space is limited due to catering, so please claim your seat today!🔗Click Here to Register & RSVP Today:Inclusive Hiring Community Conversation Registration – Fill out formAccommodations requests can be made upon registration. For questions or more information, please contact Dawn at 715-319-3626 or dawn@indigowl.org.

events.title: Light the Horizon
events.address: 7210 Fremont St,, Duluth, MN 55807-1854, United States
events.description: Light the Horizon On Thursday, October 15, from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m., we're transforming the Lake Superior Zoo into a glowing experience filled with luminary-lit pathways, live music, local food vendors, wellbeing activities, and opportunities to connect with others. Inspired by Project Horizon, this free community event celebrates the power of mental wellbeing and the impact we can make when we come together.What to Expect:- Free admission- Luminary walk- Live music- Food trucks- Wellbeing activities- Community connectionMental wellbeing shines brightest when communities come together. Every light along the pathway represents hope, connection, and the positive impact we can make when we support one another. Through Project Horizon, Members is helping create opportunities that foster mental wellbeing, strengthen relationships, and inspire positive change throughout our communities.

events.title: John H. Howe, Frank Lloyd Wright’s Architect presented by Old-Brule Heritage Society
events.description: Video presentation on John H. Howe, Frank Lloyd Wright’s Architect Local filmmakers Rob Barros and Keri Schult share stories of the life, clients, and beautiful architectural drawings by one of Frank Lloyd Wright’s most prolific draftsmen, John H. Howe. In this beautifully edited hour-long documentary, engaging interviews and music by Rick Wakeman invite you to share in creativity. Step into a different way of thinking about the spaces in which we live.

events.title: Ghost in the Gallery
events.venue: Richard I. Bong Veterans Historical Center
events.description: Ghosts in the Bong Center Museum Galleries! This Halloween season, the Bong Veterans Museum invites you to experience our museum in a whole new light. On October 24th, you can alter your vision and get spooky if you choose. The galleries will take on a mysterious atmosphere; visitors of all ages are welcome to wander through exhibits where history and imagination blur. Our mannequins have always stood watch, but during this special event you may find yourself asking—are they moving, or is it just the season playing tricks on you?Families can enjoy a mild, sensory-friendly adventure designed to spark curiosity without ever overwhelming younger visitors. For those who prefer a gentler experience, accommodations will be made to ensure everyone can participate at their own comfort level.This isn’t a haunted house—it’s a chance to celebrate the spooky season in a unique, educational, and welcoming environment. Discover the secrets of our mannequins, share in the fun of Halloween with your loved ones, and see the Bong Center like you’ve never seen it before. Regular admission applies.

events.title: Work Smarter, Not Harder: Session 3
events.description: Session 3 will dig into practical ways to make AI and the technology you already use work harder for you. We’ll explore AI notetaking apps, ways to get more out of Google Workspace, and useful AI integrations that can help streamline meetings, communication, organization, and everyday workflows. As always, the goal is practical, approachable learning with tools you can actually put to use. Joined us before? Come back and keep building on what we started. Never been? No problem at all. You can jump in here without feeling behind – we’re all still figuring it out together. Facilitators: Turns out – all of us! Guided by Abby Oxborough, Founder of The Leadership Lodge, these sessions tap into the collective knowledge in the room sharing technology hacks, practical ideas, and plenty of ah-ha moments! Bring your laptop or device to this session as we dig a bit deeper into hands-on learning! No cost to participate. Registration required: Register Here

events.title: Lunch-N-Learn-Retirement Ready: Understanding Employer Requirements & Options
events.description: Wednesday, October 21 11:15 buffet, 11:30 – 1:00 Lunch-N-Learn Chamber members are Free; Non-Chamber members $20. Minnesota retirement savings requirements are changing. Understand the requirement. Explore your options. Make the choice that works for your business. The Minnesota Secure Choice Retirement Program will discuss the requirements for Minnesota employers under state statute. This will include the compliance and rollout timelines, employer responsibilities, and a breakdown of the Program benefits for Minnesota workers and employers. Learn how a Pooled Employer Plan (PEP) through Edward Jones Investments can help Chamber members offer a qualified retirement plan with simplified administration, fiduciary support, and potential cost savings, so you can spend more time focused on growing your business. Registration Required! To register as a Chamber member, you must use a GrowthZone log in. If you do not have one, you can ask your admin, or contact the Chamber. Register here: REGISTRATION Brought to you by:

events.title: Photo Submission Contest – 2027 Area Directory
events.description: We’re looking for stunning outdoor photos that capture the beauty, culture, and spirit of Itasca County! Submit your best vertical (portrait orientation) shots for a chance to be featured in our 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory and win Chamber Bucks to be used at any Chamber member business! Prizes 1st Place: $250 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured on the cover of the 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory Photos used inside the Directory: $25 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured inside the Directory Photo Submission Guidelines Orientation: Photos must be portrait (vertical) to fit the Directory cover layout. Location: All photos must be taken outdoors in Itasca County, MN. Content: Highlight scenic landscapes, seasonal beauty, outdoor recreation, our culture, or local landmarks. People may be included but avoid close-ups. Image Quality: High-resolution photos (300 DPI minimum) preferred; smartphone photos accepted if they meet quality standards. Branding: No visible brand names, logos, or watermarks. If a selected photo contains brand logos, they will be digitally removed. Original Work: You must be the original photographer and hold full rights to the image. Deadline for Submissions Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM CST How to Submit Click this link: Photo Submission Form Limit 5 photo entries per person. Judging Criteria Photos will be evaluated based upon: Uniquely highlighting the natural beauty and essence of our topography and landscape, culture, and/or local landmarks. Relevance to tourism and the outdoor Itasca County experience Originality Composition & visual impact Ability to achieve photo quality and clarity Disclaimers By entering this contest and submitting photo(s), you grant the Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use your submitted photo(s) in the Directory and related marketing materials (print, web, social media, etc.) used in promotion of our area. events.title: Chamber Board Member Interest
events.description: There’s a Seat at the Table. Could It Be Yours? LOOKING FOR LEADERS: Who care about business. Who care about our community. Who want to help shape what comes next. The Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce is accepting applications for upcoming seats on its Board of Directors. Serving on the Chamber Board is an opportunity to bring your perspective to the table, help guide the priorities and direction of the organization, and be part of conversations that impact businesses throughout our area. Why Serve? As a Chamber Board member, you will have the opportunity to: • Help shape Chamber priorities, programs, and advocacy efforts. • Represent the perspectives and needs of our business community. • Build relationships with business and community leaders. • Contribute your experience, ideas, and perspective to the Chamber’s future. • Help strengthen the business environment in the Grand Rapids area. Who Are We Looking For? We are looking for engaged, thoughtful leaders who care about business and our community and are willing to actively participate in the work of the Chamber. Applicants must be affiliated with an active Chamber member business or organization, or hold an individual Chamber membership. We welcome applicants from different industries, backgrounds, business sizes, and areas of experience who can bring valuable perspectives to the table. What Do We Need From You? You do not need to have prior board experience or be an expert on every issue facing our business community. We are looking for Board members who are willing to: • Show up and participate in Board discussions and decisions. • Ask questions and bring your perspective to the table. • Respond to Board email inquiries, including time-sensitive votes and requests for input. • Represent the Chamber and its membership in a positive and professional way. • Participate in and volunteer at Chamber events, as you are able. What Is the Commitment? Board terms are available for three years. The Board meets eigh

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: City Council Meeting
events.description: In-Person Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meetings are open to the public and held in council chambers at the Proctor Area Community Center (PACC) 100 Pionk Drive Proctor, MN. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6. Remote Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meeting is available remotely via YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@trac7298/streams. Public comments may also be submitted in advance of the meeting to cityhall@proctormn.gov up to 3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting with the e-mail title “City Council Meeting.” All comments are public data

events.title: General Election Public Accuracy Test
events.description: CITY OF PROCTOR 2026 GENERAL ELECTION PUBLIC ACCURACY TEST Notice is hereby given the City of Proctor public test of the tabulating equipment and electronic ballot marking device will be conducted at the Proctor Area Community Center (PACC) 100 Pionk Drive, Proctor on Thursday October 22, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. for 2026 General Election. The testing is open to the public. The voting system will be tested to ascertain the system will correctly mark ballots and count the votes cast for all candidates.

events.title: National First Responder Day
events.description: National First Responders Day on October 28 recognizes the heroic men and women who make it their business to take immediate action when disaster strikes. Not sure what a first responder does? Just think about 9/11 for a moment. Firefighters, police, paramedics, and more — rushing into Lower Manhattan. Whether you’ve had your own emergency or not, it’s not hard to understand and appreciate the dangerous and difficult work they do.

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: General Election
events.description: 2026 GENERAL ELECTION NOTICE The 2026 State General Election will be held on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polling places will be open from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Voters who are in line by 8:00 PM are still eligible to vote. Absentee voting for the General Election began on September 18, 2026. Minnesota voters may vote by mail or in person before Election Day. Residents can use the Minnesota Secretary of State’s website to: Find their polling location Register to vote View a sample ballot Request an absentee ballot Track an absentee ballot Minnesota Votes - Election Information Minnesota also allows eligible voters to register or update their voter registration at their polling place on Election Day. For additional election information, please contact the City Clerk at (218) 749-3579 or visit the Minnesota Secretary of State’s website.

events.title: Celebrity Dance Challenge
events.description: 2026 marks the 20th Anniversary of Minnesota Ballet’s Celebrity Dance Challenge, an annual fundraising event that pairs local celebrities with professional dancers from the company for a fun and competitive evening of dance. Participants perform in a range of styles—such as ballroom, jazz, and contemporary—and audience members vote for their favorites. The event includes a social hour, refreshments, and a high-energy show. Social hour with appetizers and cash bar starts at 5:30; performance at 7:00 pm in the Depot Theatre. Proceeds from the Celebrity Dance Challenge support the Minnesota Ballet’s educational programs and its professional dance company, helping sustain its mission of artistic excellence and community engagement.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
events.description: Karl von Rabenau’s original choreography transforms Washington Irving’s legendary ghost story into the ultimate Halloween weekend event — a tale of rivalry, romance, and one very unforgettable ride through Sleepy Hollow. Performance at 7:00 pm on October 30, 2026 and 3:00 pm on October 31-November 1, 2026, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: Holiday High Tea
events.venue: The Great Hall at the Depot
events.description: ✨ Event Highlights: • Classic English Tea Service: Assorted sandwiches, sweets, scones and tea • Cash Bar: Specialty holiday-themed cocktails • Live Entertainment: A narrated synopsis of The Nutcracker by Minnesota Ballet dancers • Craft Corner: Decorate your own gingerbread cookie • Photo Station: Pose with ballerinas and Nutcracker characters in a turn-of-the-century-inspired setting • Discounted Minnesota Ballet merchandise & tickets available onsite 🎄 Special Offer for Families Receive $5 off children’s tickets when you purchase two or more using promo code TEA4THREE at checkout! 💎VIP Upgrades Available Treat yourself or someone special to the VIP experience, featuring: Priority seating at a private table A complimentary cocktail or mocktail A nutcracker-themed souvenir/toy Whether you’re continuing a family tradition or creating a new one, the Holiday High Tea with the Minnesota Ballet is a heartwarming way to celebrate the season.

events.title: The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale
events.description: The holiday tradition that leaves every audience spellbound — this season featuring Tchaikovsky’s beloved score performed live by the Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra. Performance at 7:00 pm on December 11, and 3:00 pm on December 12-13, 2026, at DECC’s Symphony Hall. Tickets available through Ticketmaster, or save more than $20/ticket in fees by calling the Minnesota Ballet Box Office (218-733-7570) to reserve your seats.

events.title: Coppelia
events.description: One of the most beloved comic ballets of the 19th century, Coppélia tells the story of the clever and spirited Swanilda, who outwits an eccentric toymaker and wins back her wayward fiancé — all with irresistible charm and Léo Delibes’ glorious score. Pure joy from start to finish, and a perfect introduction to ballet for the whole family. Performance at 7:00 pm on March 12 and 3:00 pm on March 13-14, 2027, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: Figure Drawing Open Studio – September 2026
events.description: Artists must individually register online for each session. Check-in at the door is required. Attendees must be 18+ Location details The Lincoln Park Building’s Great Room is a multipurpose art-making classroom space with movable work tables, chairs, easels, and drawing horses, framed by two massive arched windows and a high ceiling.

events.title: Weekly Afternoon Open Studio
events.description: $5 Members ($10 Non-Members) Weekly open studios are FREE for DAI members at Collector, Contributing, and Benefactor levels Bring your own supplies and projects to connect with others while you create. Each session includes an optional end-of-session group critique in the final half-hour. No clay studio access. When you arrive, check in with DAI team member or facilitator and sign in on the sign up sheet. The DAI will track the number of sessions you attend. Scholarships are available. Please email jswitters@duluthartinstitute.org for more information.
