events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🚗📍 Please use the Winter Admissions parking lot/entrance and meet up with the rest of the group in the Dining Room! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Fall Color Shuttle Tour
events.description: 🚐 Fall Color Shuttle Van Tours 🍁 ⏰This Outing: Thursday, October 8 | 5:00pm 💸 Pricing: MDC Member: $10.00; Nonmember: $15.00 🔗 Register Online: Click here! Experience the splendor of northeastern Minnesota’s fall season while learning about the area’s rich mining history! This fall color shuttle van tour takes you around the Glen Mine Pit Lake, stopping at picturesque vistas and historic spots where your guide will tell you stories about the unique reclaimed industrial landscape that surrounds you. 🍂🌲 Each tour lasts an hour. There is limited walking during the stops, so please wear sturdy shoes. Remember to charge your cell phone beforehand! You’ll want to take selfies and scenic shots to share with your friends and on social media. 📸 🗓️ Full Schedule: Thursday, September 24 | 5:00pm Saturday, September 26 | 11:00am, 2:00pm Thursday, October 1 | 5:00pm Saturday, October 3 | 11:00am, 2:00pm Thursday, October 8 | 5:00pm Saturday, October 10 | 11:00am, 2:00pm

events.title: Life Cycles of Iron in Art and the Landscape
events.description: 📅 Thursday, October 15, 2026 ⏰ 5:30–8:00pm 📍 MDC’s Dining Room 💲 FREE and open to all What happens when the iron beneath our feet becomes part of the art around us? Join MDC Museum & Research Center Director Allyse Freeman and painter, material researcher, and educator Elisabeth Heying for an engaging, hands-on exploration of the many life cycles of iron in art and the landscape. The evening begins with Allison MJ Collins, a representative from CHAIR, sharing how the arts are shaping the Iron Range, followed by Allyse with a brief introduction to the history and landscape of the region. Then, Elisabeth will take you on an experimental journey through the many forms and uses of iron in artmaking—from raw steel to iron oxide-based earth pigments. Watch a live demonstration of how natural minerals can be transformed into pigments and then made into paint! 🎨 Hands-on activities will include: Creating oxidation drawings on steel plates Painting with red earth pigments from the Minnesota Iron Range Exploring the connection between art, science, minerals and the landscape around us Part show-and-tell, part cooking show, part science lesson, and part art class, this unique experimental workshop invites participants to connect with the material and landscape of their home through creative experimentation. 🍴 Complimentary appetizers included! 🍹 Cash bar available! Event Schedule 5:30–6:00pm: Social hour & arrival 6:00–6:30pm: Presentations by Allison MJ Collins and Allyse Freeman 6:30–8:00pm: Experimental art workshop with Elisabeth Heying This activity is made possible by the voters of Minnesota through a grant from the Minnesota State Arts Board, thanks to a legislative appropriation from the arts and cultural heritage fund.

events.title: Family Discovery Day: International Archaeology Day
events.description: 🏺 Family Discovery Day: International Archaeology Day 📅 Saturday, October 17 ⏰ 11:00am–4:00pm 📍 Minnesota Discovery Center 💸 FREE Admission Join us for a free day of family fun as we celebrate International Archaeology Day at the Minnesota Discovery Center, featuring a FREE screening of Dora and the Lost City of Gold and hands-on archaeology activities for all ages! From 11:00am–2:00pm, enjoy archaeology activity stations in Taconite Square designed for explorers of all ages: 🥽 Experience the science of archaeology through VR technology 🪣 Sift for buried artifacts at a dig station 🍽️ Piece together broken plates like a real archaeologist 🪨 Learn about flintknapping 🏹 Try your hand at throwing an atlatl at a (cutout) bison Then, from 2:00-3:45pm, head to our theater for a FREE screening of Dora and the Lost City of Gold! Follow Dora and her friends on an adventure to save her parents and uncover the mystery of a lost Incan civilization. 🍿 Popcorn will be available for purchase for just $1 per bag. Whether you’re a budding archaeologist or simply looking for a fun family outing, there’s something for everyone to discover. Come explore, experiment, and uncover the past—one discovery at a time!

events.title: Flashlight Clueseum
events.description: 📅 Dates: October 23 & 30 ⏰ Time: 7:30-9:30pm (both times) 👤 Age Range: 13+ 💵 Cost: $13 for MDC Members; $15 for Nonmembers ❗ Takes place in the dark with low lighting! 🎟️ Click to get tickets for the Oct. 23 game! A murder has taken place at MDC, and it’s up to you to solve it! You have a set of clues, a headlamp, and an hour to (1) find the body, (2) uncover the murder weapon, and (3) ascertain who committed this dastardly crime. If you like spooky atmospheres, solving riddles, the movie Night at the Museum, and the boardgame Clue, this after-hours whodunnit is for you. Event Schedule 👋 7:30pm: Check in 🔦 8:00pm: The game is afoot! 🤔 9:00pm: Time’s up! The mystery is revealed... 🌛 9:30pm: Wrap up and say goodnight This is an alcohol-free event. Complimentary water, juice, and light snacks are provided. The game takes place in the dark and has some ~spooky~ themes, so it might not be appropriate for folks with sensory issues and children who are easily frightened. 👻 Halloween costumes are encouraged!

events.description: Peer into the past with convenient extended Research Center hours on October 29, 2026! During Late Night in the Research Center, the RC will be open from 10:00am to 8:00pm. Visiting the RC is always FREE!

events.title: The Research Center Presents: Ryan Vine’s The Cave: Poetry Reading & Book Signing
events.description: The Research Center Presents: Ryan Vine’s The Cave: Poetry Reading & Book Signing 🗓️ Date: Thursday, October 29 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 📍 Place: MDC’s Theater 💸 Cost: FREE On Thursday, October 29 from 5:00-7:30pm, come listen to one of Minnesota’s most celebrated modern poets—Ryan Vine! Ryan will be reading from his latest poetry collection, The Cave, which explores the topics of fatherhood, generational trauma, and the ways place and lineage connect. It has been named one of the “Best Poetry Books of 2025” by the California Review of Books and “Top 5 of 2025” by Zenith Bookstore in Duluth, MN. Ryan was born and raised on the backwaters of the St. Louis River in the Fond Du Lac neighborhood of western Duluth. Along with being a poet, he is also a professor of English at the College of St. Scholastica. His honors include the Northeastern Minnesota Book Award, the Weldon Kees Award, the Robert Watson Poetry Prize, and more. Vine’s haunting meditations on fatherhood, for example, are as profound and enduring as any I’ve ever read. This is manly work, utterly masterful, and deeply moving.” — Connie Wanek “These poems are as indelible as scars—and just as full of ancient wisdom. events.title: Flashlight Clueseum
events.description: 📅 Dates: October 23 & 30 ⏰ Time: 7:30-9:30pm (both times) 👤 Age Range: 13+ 💵 Cost: $13 for MDC Members; $15 for Nonmembers ❗ Takes place in the dark with low lighting! 🎟️ Click to get tickets for the Oct. 30 game! A murder has taken place at MDC, and it’s up to you to solve it! You have a set of clues, a headlamp, and an hour to (1) find the body, (2) uncover the murder weapon, and (3) ascertain who committed this dastardly crime. If you like spooky atmospheres, solving riddles, the movie Night at the Museum, and the boardgame Clue, this after-hours whodunnit is for you. Event Schedule 👋 7:30pm: Check in 🔦 8:00pm: The game is afoot! 🤔 9:00pm: Time’s up! The mystery is revealed... 🌛 9:30pm: Wrap up and say goodnight This is an alcohol-free event. Complimentary water, juice, and light snacks are provided. The game takes place in the dark and has some ~spooky~ themes, so it might not be appropriate for folks with sensory issues and children who are easily frightened. 👻 Halloween costumes are encouraged!

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🚗📍 Please use the Winter Admissions parking lot/entrance and meet up with the rest of the group in the Dining Room! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class
events.description: Intrigue Chocolate Tasting Class 📅 Date: November 12 ⏰ Time: 5:00-7:30pm 💵 Price: $48 (+ $2 processing fee) 🎟️ Register online: Click here! Indulge your sweet tooth with a 1-hour tasting and education session with local chocolate makers! During this class, you’ll delve into the science of flavor, gain insight into the chocolate-making process, and taste your way through various chocolate products (cacao tea, roasted cacao beans, and six different chocolate bars) with Aaron Barthel and Karl Mueller, co-owners of Intrigue Chocolate in downtown Chisholm, MN. 🍫☕🤤 About Aaron: Raised in Minnesota, Aaron has worn many hats throughout his life—he’s been a farmer, a botanist, a brewer, a baker, a chef, and a chocolate maker. He’s passionate about small-batch craft chocolate, and he loves experimenting with fruits, herbs, and spices. About Karl: Karl has an entrepreneurial spirit dedicated to taking on what he describes as the ultimate career challenge—building a sustainable and ethical business in the notoriously difficult industry of craft chocolate. He’s also interested in history, culture, and generally making the world a better place. Event Schedule: 🍸 5:00pm—Arrive, mingle, sip cocktails and mocktails 👨🏻‍🏫 5:30pm—Class starts 👏 6:30pm—Class ends 💸 7:00pm—Grab another drink, peruse additional chocolate merch 👋 7:30pm—Say goodbye to Aaron and Karl; take some time to explore the Museum before MDC closes Special note: Museum admission is always free from 4:00-8:00pm on Thursdays, so you can explore the exhibits and grounds before/after the class. There will also be a cash bar and extra snacks for purchase!

events.description: We’re handing out a mix of houseplants during Plant Bingo! Whether you’re a plant pro or just looking to grow your collection, everyone’s welcome. events.title: Guided Watercolor | Rainbow Trout Trio
events.description: Join Jordan Larson on Sunday, October 11 at 2 PM in the taproom for an afternoon of watercolor painting. You’ll be painting three trout in one painting, inspired by Jordan’s best-selling piece, “Lakeside.” She’ll walk you through the painting step by step, from blending and layering to washes and texture, while leaving plenty of room to make it your own. No watercolor experience needed. Jordan will guide you through it, and all of the supplies and instruction are included. Tickets are $52 per person, and the class will run for a little over two hours. Grab a cider, settle in, and paint some trout.

events.description: Monthly Trivia Night with Trivia Mafia Put your knowledge to the test at Castle Danger Brewery’s Monthly Trivia Night, happening every first Tuesday of the month at 6pm. Trivia Mafia keeps the questions fresh, challenging, and entertaining—so whether you’re a seasoned trivia buff or just in it for the laughs, there’s something for everyone.

events.title: The Rainy Rose Food Trailer
events.description: Named after their daughters’ middle names, The Rainy Rose is a family-run food trailer owned by Mike and Amy Wahlman. This local favorite brings bold, Mexican-inspired comfort food to the North Shore — crafted with heart, heritage, and serious flavor. From crispy chimichangas and birria tacos to loaded nachos and their fan-favorite Cuban sandwich, the menu at The Rainy Rose offers something for everyone, including delicious jackfruit options for plant-based eaters. Every dish is made from scratch and rooted in Mike’s 20+ years of culinary experience and passion. So what are you waiting for? Grab a bite today! events.title: Fresh Hop Fest
events.description: Fresh Hop Fest Fresh Hop Fest is back at the Castle Danger Brewery Taproom on Saturday, October 17 from 11:00 AM–6:00 PM! Celebrate hop harvest season with us at the taproom! Fresh Hop Fest is a full day of fresh beer, live music, food, and fall fun. We’ll be pouring taproom-only fresh hop beer releases, brewed with freshly harvested hops to capture bright, vibrant hop flavors at their peak. Fresh Hop Beer Fresh Hop Pale Ale with Strata Hops Fresh Hop Mosaic IPA Fresh Hop Hazy IPA with Krush Hops Live Music All Day 11:00 AM–1:00 PM | Northeast Timberland Band 1:30–3:30 PM | Shorething 4:00–6:00 PM | Squid City Slingers Food Baptism River Barbecue will be serving up the goods throughout the event. Fall Fun Gourd Painting Celebrate fall by getting creative with guided gourd painting led by artist Eric Klepinger. Make your own harvest-season creation while enjoying the festivities. Mobile Zoo | 1:00–4:00 PM Cook’s Country Connection is bringing the farm to Fresh Hop Fest! Stop by between 1:00 and 4:00 PM for a unique mobile zoo experience featuring friendly animals including a llama, alpaca, mini horse, mini donkey, and goats. It’s a fun, hands-on addition to the festival for kids, families, and animal lovers of all ages. Hop Education Ever wonder what hops actually look, smell, and feel like before they make their way into your pint? Stop by our Hop Education area to see and smell real hops used in the brewing process, learn more about what different hop varieties contribute to beer, and ask questions about how we turn fresh hops into Fresh Hop beer. Hop Trivia Think you know your hops? Put your hop knowledge to the test with Hop Trivia Whether you’re a seasoned craft beer fan or just learning the difference between Strata, Mosaic, and Krush, come see how much you know. Local Vendors Shop and explore local vendors throughout Fresh Hop Fest, including: Wild Kidd Design Little Waldo Farms Agate Acres Grab a beer, browse local goods, meet the makers, and enjoy a fall aft

events.title: Live Music: Squid City Slingers
events.description: Squid City Slingers are a high-energy Minnesota trio blending bluegrass, folk, country, and gypsy jazz into a sound that’s equal parts foot-stomping and heartfelt. Featuring driving stand-up bass, fiery fiddle, and flat-picking guitar, the band has built a growing following across the Twin Cities and Twin Ports through a mix of rich harmonies, original songs, and carefully selected covers. The group has performed at venues and festivals across the Midwest including Bent Paddle, Earth Rider, Gunflint Tavern, Bluegrass on the Black Festival, SquidFest, and the Minnesota Musician Showcase at Mall of America. With appearances on regional radio, television, podcasts, and an expanding festival schedule, Squid City Slingers continue to establish themselves as one of the Midwest’s rising acoustic acts. Their EP, Harbors & Highways, showcases the band’s Northwoods-inspired songwriting and energetic live sound.

events.title: Brother Ali with DJ Abilities
events.description: Brother Ali is a respected Hip Hop artist, speaker, and community leader. His two-decade resume includes ten critically-acclaimed albums, mentorships with iconic Hip Hop legends Chuck D and Rakim, and performances on late night shows with Jimmy Fallon and Conan O’Brien.His provocative and uplifting brand of Hip Hop has earned him coveted press features like Rolling Stone’s 40th anniversary edition and Source Magazine’s “Hip Hop Quotables”, while his outspoken social justice message has landed him on government watch lists. He’s also lectured at universities from Princeton to Stanford and delivered the keynote address at the Nobel Peace Prize Forum.When he’s not rocking the mic at Coachella or being arrested for civil disobedience in support of marginalized communities, Brother Ali travels the world learning and teaching Islamic Spirituality under some of today’s most renowned teachers. In addition to leading worship services and classes, he co-founded The Gemali Project, an organization that helps Muslim converts and spiritual seekers access the beauty of the Islamic tradition. Brother Ali recently launched The Travelers Podcast from his new home in Istanbul, exploring life’s journey with cultural, spiritual, and thought leaders from across the globe.

events.title: Fall Equinox Yoga Retreat
events.description: Register Now Gather. Nourish. Restore Breathe in the crisp northern air, feel the earth beneath your feet, and settle into a slower rhythm as autumn unfolds along Minnesota’s North Shore. This retreat offers space to pause and honor the transition into a new season through movement, stillness, and self-discovery. Wander among the trees, breathe deeply, stretch gently, and explore guided prompts that help you release what no longer serves you while setting intentions for the months ahead. This Retreat is for you if you’re ready to: • Slow down and reset • Spend intentional time in nature • Connect with like-minded community • Nourish your body with movement and food • Embrace the grounding energy of fall About the Instructor: Rewa Giroux-DumasRewa Zen Yoga and WellnessRYT 500 Growing up I can remember being outside, regardless of the weather. It was a place where I was most creative, felt safe and at home. To this day, when I find myself out of balance, I seek time to connect to nature. I found Yoga while healing from a back injury. Active most of my life, and a bit competitive, took a toll on my body. Through the practice of Yoga I learned strength, steadiness, surrender and balance in my life in addition to compassion toward myself. I enjoy guiding a fun, breath centered practice that encourages exploration of the body, breath and heart. My teachings draw from over 25 years of study and practice in the areas of health, wellness, yoga and mindfulness. The practice is one that meets you just as you are, right now. It invites a quiet exploration into courage, strength and renewal. Get ready to experience one, or more, of those AH-HA moments. Instruction, meals and lodging included. Private room options are available for an additional fee during registration. REGISTER NOW Lodging Information Directions to Wolf Ridge

events.title: Retreat for Naturalists
events.description: Retreat for Naturalists Register Now Connect. Explore. Learn. Join us at Wolf Ridge for a one-of-a-kind gathering where naturalists of all experience levels come together to explore, learn, and connect in Minnesota’s North Woods. Over the course of the event, you’ll experience hands-on sessions across Wolf Ridge’s 2,000-acre campus, our Field Station on the shores of Lake Superior, and the surrounding Superior National Forest. Learn from Wolf Ridge Naturalists, join peer-led explorations, or simply spend time discovering the landscape alongside others who share your curiosity about the natural world. Whether you’re a seasoned field naturalist or just beginning your journey, you’ll find opportunities to: Explore diverse habitats through guided field sessions and outdoor activities. Learn from experienced Wolf Ridge Naturalists and fellow participants. Meet new friends and build connections with a welcoming community of nature enthusiasts. Share ideas, observations, and expertise with others who are passionate about the North Shore and the natural world. Gather each evening for inspiring presentations, conversations, and community. Come ready to discover new places, deepen your knowledge, and be part of a vibrant community of lifelong learners in one of the Midwest’s most remarkable landscapes. ***If you are attending and interested in leading a session,request so in advance by emailing Charlie.Pavlisich@wolf-ridge.org Register Now

events.title: Mt. Telemark Enduro
events.description: The Mt. Telemark Enduro is for riders looking for a challenge on the new trails at Mt. Telemark Village. Each category will complete 3 or 4 timed, downhill sections. All riders will ride uphill, untimed.

events.title: Turkey Birkie
events.description: The Turkey Birkie Ski Festival is the perfect opportunity to glide on early snow, take a lesson, and simply enjoy a day on skis in the great north woods!

events.title: Gitchi Gami Games
events.description: Get ready for the 2026 Gitchi Gami Games! We’re proud to host the Salomon CXC Cup. It will be an epic weekend of early season racing in Cable, WI at Mt. Telemark Village!

events.title: 2027 U.S. Cross-Country National Championships
events.description: Join the Nation’s Top Cross-Country Skiers in Cable, WI for a week of world-class competition.

events.title: Seeley Hills Classic
events.description: Ski the historic Seeley Hills Classic and take part in a rich Northwoods ski tradition. The winding, wooded classic ski race is the second-largest annual classic cross-country ski event held on the Birkebeiner Trail.

events.title: Ski de She Camp & Race
events.description: Ski de She is a time for women to come together to expand their skills, build race confidence, and connect with fellow female skiers. Choose to attend our 3-day camp or compete in the adjoining race, or both! Ski with friends. Ski for health. Ski with confidence.

events.title: 2027 American Birkebeiner Ski Week Events
events.description: Be a part of a legend! The Slumberland American Birkebeiner is North America’s largest and most prestigious cross-country ski race. Skiers make their way from Cable to Hayward, WI, on the legendary Birkie Trail, finishing on the snow-covered Main Street of Hayward, WI. Enjoy a week full of racing, live music, food, and ski events in the Northwoods. An estimated 40,000 skiers & spectators will attend Birkie week festivities. Don’t miss it!

events.title: Fat Bike Birkie
events.description: The 2027 Fat Bike Birkie is the premier on-snow bike event in North America. Riders test their skill and endurance on the professionally groomed American Birkebeiner Ski Trail! Choose from 3 distances: The Big Fat 47K, The Half Fat 21K, and the un-timed Fun Fat 10K Tour – there is something for every rider!

events.title: Lunch & Learn- Retirement Plans Reimagined
events.description: LOCAL BUSINESSES—JOIN US FOR OUR NEXT LUNCH & LEARN! The Hibbing Area Chamber of Commerce invites you to an informative session designed to help local employers better understand retirement planning and the latest changes impacting businesses. Retirement Plans Reimagined: Navigating SECURE 2.0 and What Every Local Employer Should Know Thursday, October 1 11:30 AM–12:30 PM Red Rock Suites Conference Room FREE TO ATTEND! Space is limited, so be sure to RSVP today. We hope to see you there!
